Maybe rule: There is a colored line/barrier spanning full dimension. The other object is moved to the opposite edge perpendicular? Let's see.

Maybe rule: move shape in direction "away from" the separator if separator is at starting side? Wait:
- Separator at bottom, object originally top-left, move right (not away vertical upward). Maybe because separator horizontal, use horizontal axis. If line at bottom, move to right edge; if line at top, move to left edge. That's like rotate? 
- Separator at right, object originally top-left, move down. For vertical line, if line at right, move to bottom? What if left? unknown.

Maybe consider line as an arrow? Full row/column of a color indicates a wall. The object is pushed away from wall along perpendicular? Thus rule: translate shape to one of container edges, preserving orientation. Which edge? Need infer from line position and maybe shape initial location.

So if line is horizontal, move horizontally; if vertical, move vertically. Direction? For horizontal line at bottom, move right. For horizontal line at top, move left. For vertical line at right, move down. Need determine direction maybe by side of line: bottom -> right, top -> left, right -> down. Maybe left -> up? It resembles mapping edge to next edge clockwise? Let's see positions: top -> left, bottom -> right, right -> bottom. These are edges in clockwise order? Top -> left (counterclockwise? On rectangle: top edge, then left, bottom, right. Top->left is CCW. Bottom->right is CCW? Edges clockwise: top->right->bottom->left. Top->left is counterclockwise. Bottom->right is counterclockwise? bottom->right is clockwise? Let's list around clockwise: top(0)->right(1)->bottom(2)->left(3)->top. bottom->right is reverse (counterclockwise? bottom(2)->right(1) is CCW? Actually clockwise decreasing? Let's define compass: N->E->S->W. top=N. N->W is CCW. S->E? S(2)->E(1) is CCW? On compass clockwise N->E->S->W. S->W? Wait E is right, S is bottom. S->E is CCW? Clockwise from S goes W, not E. So bottom->right is CCW (S->E). Right->bottom = E->S is clockwise. Inconsistent if using single rotation.

Maybe mapping edge of line to direction of movement based on shape position? Let's examine shape initial vs line. Ex1 line bottom, shape is above line. It moves right. Ex2 line top, shape below line. Moves left. Ex3 line right, shape left of line. Moves down. So if line acts as a "wall", shape moves perpendicular to wall and perhaps toward a corner determined by shape's side? Actually:

It is at left edge, so move to opposite horizontal edge (right). i.e., move along the axis perpendicular to wall, away from shape's current aligned edge toward the other edge. Since shape initially touches left edge, move to right edge.
- Line top, shape is right edge, horizontal wall. Perpendicular axis horizontal. Shape initially touches right edge, move to opposite horizontal edge (left). Yes!
- Line right, shape is top edge? Line right is vertical, perpendicular axis vertical. Shape initially touches top edge, move to opposite vertical edge (bottom). Yes!

If line is horizontal, move shape horizontally to the opposite horizontal edge from its current horizontal position/touch. If line vertical, move vertically to opposite vertical edge from its current vertical touch. More generally, line indicates which axis? Axis horizontal, which is perpendicular to horizontal line? Actually line horizontal spans x, but movement along x. Ex2 line horizontal top, shape at right edge, moved horizontally to left. Ex3 line vertical right, shape at top edge, moved vertically to bottom. Axis vertical, perpendicular to vertical line. So line orientation determines axis? Horizontal line -> move horizontally; vertical line -> move vertically. Direction is opposite from current edge along that axis. But why axis? Maybe because line is on an edge that is parallel to the movement? No, vertical line right, movement vertical parallel to line. Horizontal line top/bottom, movement horizontal parallel to line. Yes movement is parallel to the line. The shape is moved parallel to the line from one side edge to the other. The line itself is on an edge; the shape is shifted along the direction parallel to the line to the opposite edge. Direction determined by shape's current side along that parallel axis: if shape touches left, move right; if touches right, move left; if touches top, move down; if touches bottom, move up.
